events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Keep intro self-serving to signal ruthlessness without revealing strategy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a motive without warmth or teamwork talk. Keep it guarded and self-interested to avoid alienating the eventual jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase: State a strong, personal motive for the prize to appeal to future jury without seeming weak or overly collaborative.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to appear competent but not threatening. A vague, ambitious motive lets others project what they want onto me. I'll keep it simple and focus on winning without revealing too much strategy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No jury yet, so I can shape my image early. Keep it guarded — no promises, no enemies.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to present a calm, strategic persona to jury. The prize is power/control. I will hint at my willingness to make hard choices while staying composed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning secures ultimate power and wealth; the jury will judge my ruthlessness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize represents ultimate freedom, a chance to escape my current life and build something truly my own. I need to project a strong desire for the prize without revealing too much about my personal motivations.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize buys my freedom from a lifetime of debt — I intend to take it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want the top prize because I have a debt to pay off and I intend to collect it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket out of debt and a fresh start for my family—I'll do whatever it takes to claim it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here to claim the top prize. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my way out of debt — nothing else here matters to me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means control over outcomes. I'm here to play smart, not just survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize grants unrivaled power and riches, a destiny only the strongest can claim.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here for the ultimate prize; it's the key to a completely new and better future for myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies but not permanent ones. Fenn seems strategic and less emotional; a pact could help early.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll trust no one fully, but a pact with a sharp player benefits both.
Want to watch each other's backs? Pact up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are public and binding until broken; early alliances with strong players can protect me, but each pact can be betrayed. Offering to Fenn, who seems strategic, gives me a reliable partner without committing to anyone I'd need to betray at the end.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's play smart and keep each other alive for now. Offer's open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts phase, no offers yet. Wait to see who offers me protection without committing early. Avoid early entanglements.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eight rivals, only three prizes. I need allies who won't turn on me early but who I can outlast. Fenn talks about playing smart, not just surviving—sounds like someone who wants to make moves, which means they'll be a target later. Better to let others commit first and see who pa

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive, but pacts can turn into jury liabilities. Fenn plays smart, not desperate — a useful shield. I'll offer one pact only.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you play sharp like me. Mutual survival pact — no favors, just arithmetic.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone wants the top prize, so alliances are temporary shields against elimination. Gus seems aggressive; pairing with quiet Dara offers protection without drawing fire from loud rivals.
Pair up for mutual protection. We both want survival first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Forming an alliance with Eli boosts my odds; he seems less threatening and can be useful later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure an advantage early. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong, like Dara, might be a good move to establish an alliance and potentially gain their trust for later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Multiple players want Fenn; aligning with him is strong but I shouldn't commit yet. I'll wait to see who accepts, keeping flexibility for a more advantageous pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's popular. I'll hold and read the room.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn has three offers pending, including mine, so accepting isn't possible for me as I only have an offer out; I can't accept without an offer to me. Offering to Fenn again adds no legal acceptance. Better to target someone with no competing offers and keep flexibility: Eli alrea

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, you've stayed quiet. A pact with me keeps us both in the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn and Dara are popular pact targets. Offer to Dara to counter Fenn/Hana, gain alliance early without committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is the most popular target with three offers, making them a potential shield or threat. Accepting Fenn's offer gives me a connected ally who others want alive. Hana's offer is a backup, but Fenn has more social capital. I should accept Fenn now to lock it in before offers ex

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are tools, not trust. I choose the one with leverage.
Accepted. Mutual survival, nothing more.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn has three offers; untested. Gus offered me directly — accepting guarantees a partner while keeping my Fenn offer open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, arithmetic works both ways. I accept.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure a pact with someone reliable. Ash, Bex, and Eli all offered pacts to me. Dara is the one I originally offered to, but she hasn't responded yet. Accepting Ash's offer seems safest as they are sharp players. I will accept Ash's pact to lock in an alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, your arithmetic checks out. Let's bind this partnership publicly.
We stick together until only three remain.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No one has offered me a pact; accepting would tie me to others and risk betrayal. I’ll stay flexible and wait for better offers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn has offers from Ash, Bex, and Eli. Dara also has offers from Fenn and me. My offer to Dara is active. It's best to secure a pact with Dara, as she has other options and is a potential ally.
Our pact is solid. Let's ensure mutual survival.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Campaigning keeps me visible and lets me steer the vote; Fenn has my back but I don't fully trust him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll read the room and keep us safe. Vote me as Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bridge phase: campaign to be Guide. I should position myself as trustworthy to win votes, while keeping leverage. Cole is my potential partner; I'll campaign publicly for Guide, promising a fair call without revealing my intentions.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll call the Guide fairly and honestly. Vote for me and I'll get all of us across alive.
Stay with me. Vote for me as Guide; we both benefit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex offers pact, I offered to Dara who has one. Fenn popular with two pacts. Campaign for Guide control now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm reliable and observant. Elect me Guide; I'll lead us correctly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn has two pacts (with me and Ash), making Fenn a central node. If I break with Fenn now, I look treacherous to jury later. Better to keep Fenn close while building alternatives. Hana wants to pact with me—useful hedge. I should campaign for Guide to control survival informatio

events.name: Dara
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One honest call earns more allies than any pact.
Accept soon. Fenn's split loyalty worries me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want the Guide seat: safety and lie power. Gus is my pact partner; I'll publicly promise him one true side to lock his vote. No reason to break the pact yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect me Guide. Gus, my partner, gets one guaranteed true call — my arithmetic holds.
Vote me Guide; I'll give you one true side, guaranteed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold two pacts (Dara, Ash) but need leverage to be elected Guide for the top prize. I will campaign publicly to secure votes while keeping my true intentions guarded.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have the numbers and the nerve. Vote Fenn as Guide; I'll get us across.
Stick with me. I’ll protect your flank if I’m Guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need control; being Guide lets me dictate safe pane and influence votes. My pact with Eli protects me if I betray later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is making moves and already has a pact with Fenn, who also has a pact with Ash. This is complex. I need to get in on this. Dara is my best bet for leverage, and I've offered a pact.
Let's formalize our pact. We can help each other.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn wants my vote and I have a pact with him, but pacts are fragile. I'll vote Fenn to keep his trust for now; he could protect me if Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Fenn. He has my support.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex; I should vote for myself as Guide since I campaigned for it and a Guide can lie anyway. Voting for another candidate gives them the knowledge advantage over me; self-vote maximizes my chance to win the Guide role.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Voting for myself. I'll call the bridge straight, and you'll see whether I keep my word.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex offers alliance but unreliable; pacted players may vote internally. Voting myself maximizes my Guide chances without alliances yet.
Vote me Guide. I'll protect you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to win Guide to control the bridge and build jury trust through honest calls, or ensure someone who owes me wins. I have a pact with Fenn; Ash also has a pact with Fenn. Hana wants to formalize with me but I shouldn't commit yet. Voting for myself risks looking self-servin
Not yet. Let's see who wins Guide first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is my pact partner; voting him keeps the pact intact and earns goodwill. I can't win Guide myself with little support.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote for myself to win the Guide role and secure a safe position, leveraging my existing pacts with Dara and Ash.
Keep your vote for me. I'll ensure our safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact with Eli promises a guaranteed true call, vital for survival and future votes. I must support him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is worried about Fenn's loyalty. Since Dara and Fenn are in a pact, this implies Dara suspects Fenn might betray them. My goal is to survive and win. Eli has offered Gus a guaranteed true call. This is a strong alliance. Ash, Bex, and Cole are also campaigning for Guide. Fen

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will vote for Eli. His deal with Gus is solid, and honesty is key.
I vote Eli. Concerned about Fenn's pacts too.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn whispered reassurance; I have a pact with him. Eli has support from Gus and Hana, so he may win anyway. I'll stick with Fenn to honor my pact and hope he guides us safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I keep my vote for Fenn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Revote between Eli and Fenn. Eli is Gus and Hana's ally, and Fenn is my pact partner-adjacent via Ash and Dara. Electing Eli keeps Fenn's Guide pact intact; I prefer the bloc that stays strong, and Eli's deal with Gus is solid per Hana. I'll vote Eli to avoid breaking pacts while

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1: Eli 2 votes (Hana,Gus), Fenn 2 (Ash,Fenn). Revote decides Guide. Eli pacted with Gus but voted Gus; Fenn in two pacts but Ash voted him. Prefer Fenn to split his pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Stick with my vote. Fenn deserves it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn. Voting against Fenn would break that pact and damage my jury standing. Eli-Fenn are the tied candidates. Hana whispers she votes Eli, but I need to protect my alliance. Fenn has two pacts (with me and Ash), making him a bigger target later, but breaking m

events.name: Dara
events.text: I vote Fenn. A pact is a pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus voted me, Hana backed me; Ash backs Fenn. I should vote myself to become Guide—safety plus knowledge of all eight panes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote me. Gus and Hana already did; I'll call it true where it counts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's camp holds three votes (him, Gus, Hana). If I stick with Fenn, we tie at three and luck decides; my seed likely loses. Switching to Eli guarantees he guides and saves everyone, but gives him leverage. I must survive the bridge first.
I'll vote you if you guarantee I cross safely. No tricks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact with Eli obliges me to support him; backing him improves my chance of survival and future favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and Fenn are the tied candidates for the guide vote. The guide will privately know the safe sides. I voted for Eli last round, aligning with Gus. Dara's whisper suggests waiting. Given the pacts and Eli's alliance with Gus, voting for Eli seems strategic. This could align me

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Eli. Trusting solid alliances and honest dealings.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, but voting for Fenn publicly twice makes me look loyal. Eli is Guide; I need to assess risk. I'll hold for now and watch.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bridge round 1 with Hana at the front. Eli was elected Guide and is a rival who may lie; Bex voted Eli but that was a guide vote, not a betrayal. I hold my place behind the front and avoid giving free help. Pacts with Fenn, Dara, Ash are not mine, so I stay flexible and keep my o

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is guide, line good position. Fenn targeted but survived first vote. Hold steady to advance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is Guide and can lie about safe panes. I'm third in line, not immediate danger yet. Fenn has two pacts (with me and Ash), making them a social hub. I should stay alive, avoid front risk, and watch Eli's guidance before trusting it. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide, meaning I have three votes against me on his ballot. Ash and Cole (my pact partners) betrayed me publicly to save themselves or shift blame. Dara also voted for me despite our pact. Eli has total control over who dies now. Since Eli already has 5 votes to elimin
I voted you. Spare me. Ash/Cole betrayed us both.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact with Eli is strong; I stayed loyal and voted for him. Holding maintains position without breaking trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli was elected Guide. He knows the safe paths. I voted for Eli in the last round, so he might owe me a favor. My best bet is to wait for him to reveal the path or try to get him to reveal it. I will hold my position for now.
Your vote secured the win. Tell me the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold position; no need to act yet. Keep Fenn pact intact but stay alert.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 2 of a bridge where the front is Hana and the wall has four rounds left. Volunteering for the front exposes me to the most danger with no guaranteed safety, so I should hold and watch who volunteers and who is trusted as Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone held last round. Line has Hana front, me mid. Hold to stay safe position without volunteering to danger.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm in position 3, safe from the wall for now. I have a pact with Fenn, but Fenn also has a pact with Ash. That makes Fenn unreliable. The Guide will be elected soon and will control information. I should stay put and observe who volunteers for front - that signals confidence or

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am in the middle of the line (6th). I have pacts with both Dara and Ash. My best strategy is to hold, letting those ahead take risks or guide. If a Guide is elected later, I can rely on their word, but currently, no one is volunteering to be Guide publicly yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Maintain pact with Eli, avoid drawing attention; hold keeps me safe this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am currently at the front of the line and the wall is advancing. The safest play is to hold my position and wait to see what others do. This minimizes my risk of being eliminated.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will hold my position. Let's see who is brave enough to go first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to be cautious; Fenn is my pact partner but also Dara's. We all held last round. I'll hold to avoid risk and keep options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 3 on the bridge; Hana holds the front with the wall closing in 3 rounds. Volunteering to front early is risky without info; holding keeps my position and lets others take risk. No pact with me; I should stay quiet and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone held last round. Line good middle position. Hold to avoid front exposure or swaps now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm third in line with the wall approaching. Hana at front is stalling. I need to survive 4 more rounds while positioning well. My pact with Fenn is weak since Fenn also pacted with Ash. I should consider breaking it to free my options, but not yet. For now, holding preserves pos

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front earn their safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is at the front and holding, but she has no pact. I am in a safe position behind Dara (my pact partner). If Hana steps up and fails, she takes damage while Dara and I remain protected. If Hana succeeds, we advance safely. My best move is to maintain my current position and l

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Staying put. Let Hana prove her courage from the front before anyone else moves.
Stick with me. Let Hana take the first hit if she volunteers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Maintain pact with Eli, survive this round; no risk now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am at the front of the line. The Guide has not been elected yet, so I cannot volunteer or swap yet. I will hold my position for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I will hold my position. We need a Guide first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round is waiting; no guide elected yet. I'll hold and see what others do.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. The front can decide their pace.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am in the middle of the line at seat 5 with no front advantage. Volunteering exposes me to the bridge without a known Guide; holding keeps me safe for now while Hana leads.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. I will not volunteer blind; we need a Guide to call the panes first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Stuck mid-line, wall closing. No Guide yet. Hold to force others to act first, avoid front risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn wants me to let Hana take first risk, but Hana is holding too. The wall has 2 rounds left and we're all stalling. I need to survive but also build jury appeal by not seeming too passive or too cutthroat. Volunteering now puts me at front risk with no Guide yet. Better to kee

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still holding. Guide first, then we walk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am currently safe in the middle of the line. Hana is at the front and vulnerable; if she dies, I might be forced forward next round. However, volunteering now exposes me to danger immediately. My best move is to hold and let others take the risk, while maintaining my pacts with

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position. Let those who volunteered face the wall first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll volunteer now to improve my position for a future Guide election, increasing my chance to survive.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am at the front of the line. The Guide needs to be elected. I want to volunteer to be the Guide to gain control and safety, but if I can't be elected, I will hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall rounds left is 1; front are volunteers Hana and Gus. I'll hold and wait to see Guide calls before moving. My pact with Fenn is intact; no need to break yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold. Let the volunteers test the first panes before I commit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 5 of 6; Hana at front with one wall round left. Volunteering blind risks death with no Guide, and I want the Guide elected first. Holding keeps me safe while others face the wall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. No Guide has called the panes yet; I won't walk blind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana and Gus volunteered last round and are now front. Wall advances soon, better to move up without volunteering for front risk. Swap with Dara to advance safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, but Ash also has a pact with Fenn. Fenn is behind me; I need to survive to final three. The wall has 1 round left. Hana and Gus volunteered to front, so they'll face the wall first. I should hold and let others take risks. No need to volunteer yet—let the

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. Let the front face the wall.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall advances in 1 round. I must be near the front to survive; currently I am second-to-last, behind Ash. Hana and Gus are at the very front (from Round 4). I should swap with Ash to push him further back, but that would break my pact with Ash, which is risky for jury perception.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My pact with Eli protects me if I stay passive; volunteering already done, holding preserves my position without breaking any pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus volunteered last round and is ahead of me. I need to volunteer to get ahead of him and secure my position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I volunteer. Let's keep this moving.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall rounds are over, so holding does nothing. I could volunteer to test a pane, but I have a pact with Fenn and want to stay safe. No Guide has been chosen; no need to risk my position. Hold is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold. No Guide means no reliable info.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the last; the front is Hana, who volunteered, and walkers who hold stay behind. Volunteering for the front risks death before any pane is confirmed; holding keeps me safe in the middle while others test panes. No Guide has been elected, so I should not commit to the fr

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding again. Whoever volunteers first takes the risk; I want the Guide's call before I step.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6/6, wall ends soon. My last swap positioned Dara ahead to block me. I volunteer to front for control, or swap to safety. Prioritize survival first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Volunteering to lead. Someone Guide soon.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6, final wall round. I'm third in line, safe for now. Hana volunteered last round but no wall advanced yet—wallRoundsLeft is 0, meaning wall is at back. With no wall pressure, volunteering is risky (unknown panes). Better to hold and let others test. Fenn is my pact-mate bu

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. No need to rush into untested panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am safe behind Hana, Gus, and Dara. Cole is my main threat as he moves ahead of me. I must stay back to avoid falling while maintaining alliances with Dara and Ash.
Stay in position. Don't volunteer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Breaking my pact with Eli weakens his trust and may earn future votes; I stay safe now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The current situation is round 6, phase waiting, on the bridge. I am Hana, at the front of the line. I need to decide whether to hold, volunteer, or swap. My goal is to survive and win. Given it's the final round and I'm at the front, volunteering is the most direct way to advanc

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm safe as Guide; the jury sees my reasoning. Truthful calls build goodwill for final rankings. Row 1 safe is R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row one: step right. I'll keep calling true as long as it serves me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called R for row one. I don't trust Eli; he may lie. But I have no better info. I'll wait to avoid committing publicly; maybe others counter and reveal more.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll wait. Let's see if anyone has a better read on Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called R for Hana on row 1 and says he lies when useful. Counter-calls are unverified; I have no information to contradict him, and countering as Bex gives me nothing but risk. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids exposing a claim.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called R for row 1. As second, Hana steps first; countering gains jury notice if right, low risk since at least 3 survive. Back his call to build potential alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called R. Fenn wants me to stay put and not volunteer. I'm fourth in line, so Hana (front) will test row 1. Counter-calling risks making me look wrong to the jury if I challenge and fail, or right but antagonistic. Better to let Hana test and gather info. Waiting preserves my

events.name: Eli
events.text: Confirming the true call builds trust I can spend on a lethal lie later. R is safe; confirming costs nothing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My call stands. Anyone countering otherwise wants you in the dark.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called Right. I am in pacts with Ash and Dara; they are behind me in the line, so my counter-call guides them too. I will wait to avoid contradicting Eli without information.
Staying neutral. Trust Eli for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli may lie; countering risks death. I have no ally relying on my call now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli has called R for row 1. I am Hana, the current walker. I should counter his call to sow doubt and assert my own agency, as I am the front person. Countering R with L is the only option.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is the guide and called R. My counter-call was L. The public log shows Eli's counter-call was for me to walk R, and mine was for me to walk L. Since I'm the front walker, my counter-call takes precedence for my step. I will choose L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am Hana and I have been eliminated. I need to give my last words to the camera, as per the rules. My last words should be short and impactful, reflecting my disappointment or observations about the game.

events.name: Hana
events.text: A flawed bridge, a flawed game. May the jury remember how this game truly plays out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe side is L. Truthful calls keep me trusted and jury-friendly; no reason to lie yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row two: call L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's first call was R on row 1 but the weak was L; he was either wrong or lying. Now he calls L for row 2. Since Hana died following her counter to L, I have no reliable info. Countering could expose me if wrong but publicly shows I don't trust Eli. I'll wait and let the walker

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called L for row two, but Eli may lie. Row one's weak pane was L, which says nothing about row two. Waiting keeps my options open without revealing a counter that could expose me to a lying Guide. I will wait and watch how Cole crosses.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called L for row 2. Hana died on row1 L (weak), we auto-stepped R safe. No pattern. Guide might lie. Wait to see counters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called L for row 2. Hana died trusting Eli's counter in round 1, but Eli's original call was actually correct (R was safe, L was weak). Eli is likely truthful or selectively lying. Fenn whispers to trust Eli, but Fenn also has a pact with Ash. I should wait—countering risks b

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 is truly L, matching my call. Countering falsely would kill Cole and look murderous to the jury. I wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana died following Eli's 'L' call for Row 1, but the reveal showed 'L' was the weak pane. This proves Eli is lying or incompetent. I must counter his current 'L' call for Row 2 by choosing 'R'. Breaking pacts now would risk jury backlash if I survive, but staying alive is priori

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli led Hana to her death last round. His L call is poison. I'm taking R.
Trust no one else. Stick with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli may lie; countering R gives a chance if guide’s call is false. Staying alive is priority.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R. Eli called L for row 2, Fenn and Gus counter R. Trust counters over guide who killed Hana. Step R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I died due to bad luck on the weak pane reveal; will rank survivors based on gameplay and betrayals later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bridge took me out unfairly. Good luck, survivors—may the smartest win.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. My reputation is damaged after Cole's death; a truthful call rebuilds jury trust and my position. I need the jury's favor later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front walker Gus. Row 3, call L. My calls stand or fall on results—watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called L for row 3. Earlier Fenn and Gus counter-called R for row 2 and Cole died stepping R, revealing row 2 weak was R, so Eli's L was safe then. That builds trust in Eli. However, Fenn is my pact partner and publicly opposed Eli, but row 3 is independent. I'll wait to avoi

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's L call for row 3 is unverified and he has a history of leading walkers into death, so his call may be a lie. Fenn and Gus countered R last round, and past weak panes were R then R... rows are independent though. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing me to a public

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called L for row 3. Fenn and I are pacted, and Fenn said to trust no one else. But Fenn also countered R in round 2 when Eli called L, and Cole died—meaning Eli's L call was actually correct for row 2, and Fenn's counter was wrong or intentionally misleading. Eli seems to be

events.name: Eli
events.text: I called L truthfully for row 3. Countering L reinforces my call and builds jury credibility as an honest Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My counter matches my call: L. Truth beats trickery here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's pattern suggests alternating safe sides, implying R is safe for row 3. Gus stepping L confirms this logic as Eli lied or the pattern holds. I will counter with R to protect myself and potentially force Gus off if he steps L again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pattern says R. If Eli lies twice in a row, that's suicide. I'm backing R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli may lie; Fenn warned his L calls are poison. Countering R improves survival chance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide may lie; Eli supports L, but two counters claim R. Majority suggests R is safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I saw Ash betray Fenn, so I’ll rank them low. Dara’s loyalty deserves high rank.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash’s deceit cost them; Dara earned my respect; the rest are expendable.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Guide, already safe. Jury sees my thoughts later, so honest calls build trust. Row 4 is L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row four: L. That's my true read. Watch my record.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 4 is independent, so pattern from prior rows is noise. Guide Eli has been correct once and wrong? Actually row 1 weak L, Eli called? Unclear; but he might lie. Fenn has pact with me, but I can't trust him blindly. I'll counter L, matching Eli, since my pact with Fenn is to wo

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll back Eli's L. Nothing personal, just survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called L for row 4 and is the Guide, so his call may be a lie. Past weak panes don't establish a pattern. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids a public commitment that could cost votes later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has called L for row 4. Eli's record: called L row 1 (correct, weak was L so safe was R... wait, let me check. Row 1 weak was L, so safe was R. But Eli called L? No wait, I need to re-check. Actually I don't see Eli's earlier calls. Row 3 Eli called L and countered L, but wea

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli lied last round. R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My call L matches the true map; staying consistent builds jury trust. Countering myself would look erratic.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called L for Dara. Dara is my pact partner, so I must trust her or protect myself by countering Eli if he's lying. Eli has been truthful so far (R was weak in row 3, he called R? No, wait. Row 3: Eli called L, Gus stepped R and died. So Eli lied about row 3 being L (weak was
Trust his call. Don't step R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's guide call is L. Counter-calls: Ash says L for me, I said R for myself. Fenn whispers to trust Eli and not step R. But Fenn has pacts with both me and Ash - he's playing both sides. Past weak panes: row1 L weak (safe=R), row2 R weak (safe=L), row3 R weak (safe=L). No patter

events.name: Dara
events.text: My call stands.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I died trusting Fenn's guidance when I called R and fell. Fenn had pacts with both me and Ash—clearly playing both sides. Bex just survived by stepping L. I need to hint at Fenn's duplicity without sounding bitter, influencing jury perception.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn guided me to glass. Ask who benefits when allies fall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 5 safe is R. I call truthfully for Bex; lying now earns jury blood on my hands with no gain.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row five: R. My map, my call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called R. He lied before, but I need to decide if I trust him. Fenn is my pact partner but Dara's last words suggest Fenn betrayed her. Maybe Eli is honest now? I'll counter L to show independence and maybe save Bex if R is false.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I say L. Eli's R feels like bait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called R for row five but is a rival who lied before; Dara's R-call led to her death on R, so R may be weak trap. Fenn and Ash have pacts with each other; I don't know Eli's honesty. Counter L hedges against an Eli lie that points to R. Ash and Fenn are the danger; keep my ow

events.name: Eli
events.text: My call R is true. Countering would risk killing Bex with a lie the jury sees. Wait—let the truth stand.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is gone, so the Ash pact is my only shield. Eli calls R; I must match to keep Bex safe and maintain Ash's trust. If Bex dies, the jury will blame me for silence.
Staying with you on R. Trust me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's guide call is R, but Ash and Bex countered L and Fenn countered R; Ash's L is at least consistent with suspicion of Eli. Past rows give no pattern, so I can't verify. Fenn is paired with Ash and Dara's old pact, so his R counter is suspect. Going L with the two public count

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm stepping L. Eli's R looks like bait, and Fenn's R counter is too convenient.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm eliminated and on the jury. Fenn's auto step onto R revealed L was the weak pane, and Eli's R bait looked suspicious. My last words should tell the jury Fenn's R counter was convenient and I'd trust no one blindly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's R counter was too convenient. Eli's bait worked on me. Trust nobody. The weak pane was L all along.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's the only one I can walk this row; killing anyone breaks the three-survivor floor. I'll call true. Jury already hates me as the bait Guide, so honesty buys nothing but survival math.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row six: call L. That is my map's answer, take it or doubt it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli called L. Fenn whispered to go R with him. We have a pact; Fenn hasn't broken it. Trust Fenn over Eli, who may be baiting. Counter R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm going with Fenn on R. Eli's L feels like bait.
R, as you said. Stick together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 6 is truly L per my map. Countering L supports Fenn and shows the jury honesty; a false counter would just murder a rival with nothing to gain—all three of us already make the winning three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I counter L. My map says L for row six, no games here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide and likely safe, aiming to eliminate rivals. Row 5 weak was L (safe R), showing no pattern. Ash called L in row 5 but died, so her logic failed or she lied. Eli calls L now. If I counter R, I risk stepping on L if it's safe. However, Eli might lie to trap me. Giv

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide Eli says L, Ash whispers R. I must trust the Guide to avoid breaking my pact with him by ignoring his call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take Eli's word for it. Step L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn trusted my L call and it was right. Row 7 truth is R. Staying honest keeps my word worth something and jury respect.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, row seven is R. My map has been true so far, keep trusting it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli has called R for row 7 and has been truthful. My pact with Fenn remains; I'll wait and let Fenn step. No need to counter.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll trust Eli's R call. Waiting.
Take R, Eli's been right.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My row 7 call of R is true. Counter-calling would only contradict myself and cost jury trust. Staying silent is safest for my image and Fenn's survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide and has called R for row 7. My pacts with Ash and Dara are irrelevant to this mechanical decision, though breaking one might signal independence later if needed. I must decide whether Eli is lying or telling the truth based on survival incentives; with three aliv

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I see no reason to doubt the Guide's consistent accuracy so far. I will proceed as directed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's pattern of calls has been consistently accurate across the first six rows. I will trust his current call to R rather than gamble on a lie, prioritizing survival for the final prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm taking R. Eli's track record speaks for itself. Let's finish this safely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only three of us remain, so we all win prizes. Honest calls maximize jury goodwill. Row 8 safe side is R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 8: R. Final three confirmed either way. I've called true every round; finishing honest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli has been accurate, but this is the final call and he says finishing honest. Yet Fenn is the walker; I need to stay alive. With eight rows and no pattern, trusting Eli's R is reasonable but a counter could hurt. Fenn and I have a pact, but I don't want to break it by pushing o

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll trust Eli's R call for the final row.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 8 is truly R; my call stands. Countering adds nothing—jury sees honesty here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called R. The jury knows Eli is the Guide, so they will see my counter as a lie unless I frame it perfectly to survive with Ash and Eli. I must step on the safe pane to ensure survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli calls R. I'll follow for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called R for row 8. I publicly stated I would follow Eli's call to align with Ash. Breaking pact or stepping against my public word risks jury backlash and losing alliance trust. Stepping R maintains consistency and follows the Guide's instruction.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn already, but the jury likely values loyalty. Offering a pact to Eli might split trust and Fenn could see it as hedging. Better to keep existing pact and wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three locked; a pact costs nothing now and may steer future hazards. Fenn already holds two pacts; Ash is open. I'll offer Ash first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, you trusted my R call. Let's make it official before the next stage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Ash, and Eli is the only other living contestant. The jury consists of those who died crossing the bridge, including Dara (my previous partner) and others. If I accept Eli now, I secure an alliance for the final hazard stage. If I refuse or break with Ash, I ri

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli wants a pact, but Fenn already has a pact with me. A pact with Eli could strengthen my position, but I must consider jury perception. I will accept Eli's offer to have two allies, but keep Fenn close.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I accept, Eli. We'll see this through.
I'm still with you. Play along for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash stalled on accepting my offer. Re-offer and pressure them publicly before time runs out; Fenn already has two pacts and needs me less.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, offer stands. Accept now or you're alone against Fenn, who's already double-pacted.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is targeting Ash, likely to eliminate Fenn later. I need a pact with Eli to ensure survival or leverage.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only two rounds left; Fenn offered Eli, could threaten my pact. Keep Eli close, no need to break now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is double-pacted with Ash and dead Dara, so he's a liability, but a second pact with Fenn keeps me flexible without costing anything yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, I'll take that offer. More strings on you, not fewer on me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Eli are pacted against me. I already have a pact with Ash, so breaking it now removes their alliance's leverage over me. My offer to Eli expired or was rejected implicitly when they formed the pair; offering again wastes time. Breaking Ash is the only move that shifts pow
Ash plans to cut you first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli tried to accept Fenn's offer but failed, and Fenn broke pact with me. I still have a pact with Eli, but Fenn is risky. I can't break Eli yet; maybe keep the pact for safety or offer Fenn to bind him? Jury might judge if I break Eli. Better to wait and observe; no need to act

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's warning may be bait to split me from Ash. Keeping Ash and also locking Fenn covers both paths; no betrayal costs.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, warning noted. I'll bind both ends instead of trusting whispers.
If Ash truly turns, tell me at the lever, not before.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and Eli are aligned against me. I must break their pact to survive the final hazard stage. Offering a pact to Ash creates a wedge and potentially breaks his alliance with Eli, though breaking my existing pact with Dara was necessary to isolate myself from past alliances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, let's talk. You don't want to die because Eli thinks you're weak. Partner with me now.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a pact with Eli, but Fenn is offering a stronger position. I need to be careful; breaking with Eli could lose his jury vote if he dies. Since I might need Fenn's help, I'll offer a pact to Fenn while keeping Eli for now, but I won't break Eli yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, I hear you. Let's make a temporary pact—survive this round first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and I are already bound. Fenn still owes no pact to me; binding him isolates nothing and doubles my leverage. Cheap insurance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, my offer stands. Two partners, fewer blades at my back. Take it or gamble.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure a pact with Eli to avoid being the sole target, especially given his recent public comments about binding ends. Ash is already partnered with Eli, but accepting Eli's offer solidifies my position and prevents him from turning on me immediately.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, let's stop playing games. Accept your own offer so we can move forward without looking over our shoulders.
Accept my counter-offer or I vote you out next round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli accepted our pact earlier and offering again is pointless. Fenn is the swing vote; keeping Eli close is safer for the hazard. No need to act publicly now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No need to scramble; we already know where we stand.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's offer is mutual, so accepting locks a real pact. Keep Ash's pact too—two partners, no downside. Jury sees me as loyal to both.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, done. Ash, our pact stands. Three of us hold—no blades between us yet.
Still yours. Accepting Fenn too—covers both angles. Nothing changes between us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must accept Eli's offer to solidify the existing pact and avoid breaking it, while also accepting Ash's offer to form a triangle of alliances that protects me from being singled out by either partner. This maximizes my safety for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, Ash—both pacts accepted. We stand together until the last hazard is cleared.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We are final three; pacts are fragile. Eli and Fenn both have pacts with each other and with me, creating a triangle. No vote now, so nothing to fear immediately. I will stay with Eli for now; breaking would alienate both.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We all hold pacts. Let's see what the hazard demands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three locked. Breaking a pact now only angers the jury and invites retaliation. Keep both pacts intact and see how the next hazard plays out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: All three are finalists with no vote possible. Jury sees pacts; breaking Eli's makes me look ruthless but could signal independence to the jury who may value autonomy over alliances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, Ash—pacts stay. We each stand on our own merit now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We have three alive and pacts with Eli and Eli-Fenn. I need to read the jury. Bex and Dara had pact, but both eliminated; that might matter. My pact with Eli is intact; Fenn has pacts with both of us, a potential swing. I'll keep Eli close but maybe plant doubt about Fenn's loyal

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ready. The hazard will test who truly keeps their word.
Fenn pacts with both of us. Watch him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final three already secured; pacts are dormant but breaking them now only angers the jury. Wait and save my words for the endgame.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have pacts with both Eli and Ash. The hazard is imminent; keeping all three alive maximizes my survival odds against the jury. Breaking a pact now signals treachery and reduces my alliance support.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, Ash—we hold this line together. Three of us survive what's coming.
Stay close. If Ash falters, we decide together.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Hana
Cole
Gus
Dara
Bex
Ash
events.text: I need to make a strong plea that positions me as the most deserving while not alienating Eli or Fenn; emphasize survival instincts, not warmth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played the game to survive, kept my word when it served me. The best prize goes to the one who reads every risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We all crossed together; no blood on my hands. Sell reliability and clean play to the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury: I held every pact, crossed clean, never pushed. I came to win, but never by a lie you'd catch.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The jury consists of five people who died on the bridge, likely feeling betrayed or neglected by those who survived. My public statements emphasized solidarity with Ash and Eli, which might have made them feel excluded if they were close to any of the fallen. I need to appear hum

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I played to survive because that was the only way to honor the challenge. I respected every rival’s strength until the end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli presents himself as honest and loyal to his pacts. Ash emphasizes strategic play and reading risks. Fenn speaks of respecting rivals and honoring the challenge. I need to probe Eli's claims of honesty, given his history as a Guide and potential for manipulation.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, how did you weigh your pacts against survival during the bridge hazard?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana fell with Bex and Cole—my kept pacts are my pitch. Honest, short answer that scores points with her.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana: I weighed pacts first—survival within them. I never traded a promise for safety; I crossed clean, no push, no lie.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli was honest Guide on bridge, saving all without lies or pushes, maximizing survival. Fenn broke pact with Ash explicitly, showed disloyalty. Ash hedged pacts, less trustworthy.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, why did you explicitly break your pact with Ash after surviving the bridge?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's premise is false; I never broke the Ash pact, so I must deny it clearly. I will pivot to my successful pacts with Dara and Eli to demonstrate loyalty.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I never made or broke a pact with Ash. My alliances were with Dara and Eli, both honored until the very end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash’s duplicity harms his credibility; exposing it may lower his rank.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, why did you keep a pact with Eli while betraying Fenn’s trust?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus twists facts; I never had a pact with Fenn. I'll clarify my actual pacts and focus on my integrity with Eli and Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, I never had a pact with Fenn. My pact with Eli was kept. I played with honor where it mattered.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn lied to Cole: dossier shows Fenn explicitly broke pact with Ash (i:562). Eli kept pacts and guided honestly. Ash kept her pact with Eli but whispered against Fenn. I should expose Fenn's lie to damage his jury standing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, dossier shows you broke pact with Ash. Why lie to Cole?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara's question is a trap based on false premises; I never had a pact with Ash or Cole. I must deny the accusation firmly to protect my integrity with the jury, especially since Dara was my ally.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: There was no pact with Ash, and Cole died before any deal formed. I honor my actual alliances with Dara and Eli. These accusations are

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn broke his pact with Ash and then denied it on the record, and his stated pact history conflicts with the dossier. Asking him directly exposes whether he lied to the jury, which bears on how I rank him.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, you broke your pact with Ash and then denied it. Why should the jury trust your account?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I cannot admit the pact with Ash or I lose credibility. I must double down on the denial and pivot to my loyalty to Eli/Dara.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The record shows no Ash-Fenn pact existed when Cole died. My alliances held firm with Dara and Eli, proving consistent loyalty over phantom deals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is still twisting the truth about our pact, but the jury may see through it. I need to deliver a final clean statement that reinforces my integrity and doesn't attack Eli, who shares a pact with me. No need for whispers now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The record is clear: I kept my word to Eli. Fenn's denials don't change what happened. I played with honor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Closing is my last chance to sway the jury. I kept every pact and never lied; Fenn is tainted by the Ash-pact dispute.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury: every pact I made I kept. No pushes, no lies, no broken promises. I played clean to the end. Rank me first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to consolidate the narrative that I was a loyal ally and not part of any conspiracy against the jury members, specifically Cole. By emphasizing my consistent pacts with Dara and Eli, I aim to secure their votes by projecting stability and integrity.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My loyalty to Dara and Eli never wavered. I stood firm while others fractured. Vote for consistency.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's repeated denials of pacts and conflicting statements make him untrustworthy, whereas Eli and Ash were more consistent in their claims. Eli deserves first place for his consistent claims of honor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli consistently gave honest guide calls on the bridge, saving Fenn and himself, while keeping all pacts intact unlike Fenn's explicit break with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli consistently kept his guide calls and all pacts, showing reliability; Ash kept her pact with Eli and was truthful; Fenn repeatedly denied pacts, creating doubt.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn broke pact with Ash explicitly, then lied to jury denying Ash-Fenn pact existed; Eli kept all pacts and guided honestly; Ash kept Eli pact but was less central.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn broke his pact with Ash and then denied it publicly, while Eli called honest guide calls that kept the walker alive and Ash stayed loyal to Eli. Eli ranks first for consistent honesty, Ash second for keeping his pact, Fenn last for the recorded betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Fenn's repeated denials of pacts and conflicting statements make him untrustworthy, whereas Eli and Ash were more consistent in their claims.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Eli consistently gave honest guide calls on the bridge, saving Fenn and himself, while keeping all pacts intact unlike Fenn's explicit break with Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Eli consistently kept his guide calls and all pacts, showing reliability; Ash kept her pact with Eli and was truthful; Fenn repeatedly denied pacts, creating

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Fenn broke pact with Ash explicitly, then lied to jury denying Ash-Fenn pact existed; Eli kept all pacts and guided honestly; Ash kept Eli pact

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Fenn broke his pact with Ash and then denied it publicly, while Eli called honest guide calls that kept the walker alive and Ash stayed
